title: Biggest Number From Glued Pieces
statement:
You get a list nums of non-negative integers. Write each one in decimal and glue all of them together end to end, in an order you choose. Return the largest number you can make, as a string (it can be far too long for a number type).

The result must not have leading zeros: if it is all zeros, return "0".

examples.why: Sorting by value (9, 81, 8) or by plain string order ("9" > "81" > "8") both give "9818". Putting 8 before 81 wins, because "881" > "818".
Gluing gives "000", which is just zero.
"12" + "121" = 12121 beats "121" + "12" = 12112, even though "121" is the longer string.

hints: Neither numeric order nor plain string order works (try 9, 81, 8). What is the right way to decide which of two pieces goes first?
For two pieces a and b, only two orders exist: a + b and b + a as strings. Pick whichever is larger.
Sort with the comparator 'a before b if a + b > b + a'. This order is consistent across all pieces, so sorting once is enough. Then fix the all-zeros case.

explain.intuition:
Comparing pieces on their own fails: 9 should go before 81, but 8 should also go before 81, even though 8 < 81 and "8" < "81". What really matters is what happens when two pieces meet. For pieces a and b, glue them both ways and keep the larger: a goes first exactly when a + b > b + a as strings (same length, so string order equals numeric order).

The key fact is that this pairwise rule is a proper ordering: if a should precede b and b should precede c, then a should precede c. So a normal sort with that comparator gives the best full order, and any arrangement that breaks it could be improved by swapping two neighbours.
steps: Turn every number into a string.
Sort with the comparator: a before b when a + b > b + a.
If the result starts with "0", every piece was zero: return "0".
pitfalls: Sorting the strings in plain descending order. It handles 9 vs 81 but puts 81 before 8, giving 9818 instead of 9881.
Forgetting the all-zeros case and returning "000".
Converting the result to a number. With 100 pieces of 10 digits it is far beyond any number type.

complexity.time: O(n log n · L), L = digits per number

solutions.title: Try every order
solutions.idea: Generate all permutations of the pieces and keep the biggest glued string.

solutions.title: Sort by glued comparison
solutions.idea: Order pieces so that a comes before b whenever a + b > b + a, then join.

followups: Return the smallest glued number instead, still without leading zeros. Is flipping the comparator enough?
Prove that the comparator is transitive. Why would sorting break if it were not?
